4.3.2.7 Inter-ECU Response Channel Fan-Out
In the case that a SystemSignal mapped as the callSignal in a ClientServerToSignalMapping fans in from multiple ISignals and the associated returnSignal fans out to multiple ISignals, rather than sending any server response to all response ISignals, the RTE shall ensure that server responses are passed to the corresponding response ISignal based on the incoming ISignal for any given server invocation. A calling ISignal is mapped to the corresponding response ISignal by traversing the model and looking at the relevant ISignalTriggerings and PhysicalChannels. ISignals of the same PhysicalChannel that refer to a respective callSignal need to have exactly one corresponding ISignal at the same PhysicalChannel that refers to a returnSignal, where both of the SystemSignals are referenced by the same ClientServerToSignalMapping.
[SWS_Rte_04694] The RTE shall unambiguously map together a call ISignal to a response ISignal ⌈When a server runnable is configured to receive requests from multiple callers located on different ECUs, in which the signals from all callers fan-in to a single callSignal and the related response signals fan-out from a single returnSignal, the RTE shall ensure that each ISignal of the same PhysicalChannel referring to the callSignal has exactly one corresponding ISignal at the same PhysicalChannel referring to the returnSignal where both of the SystemSignals (callSignal and returnSignal) are referenced by the same ClientServerToSignalMapping.⌋ To ensure that call and return paths are unambiguous, the designer must ensure that
[constr_9395] and [constr_5274] from the AUTOSAR System Template are not violated. If these constraints do not hold, an RTE cannot disambiguate the call/response paths for inter-ECU server invocations.
[SWS_Rte_04634] ⌈The RTE generator shall raise an error if [constr_9395] or
[constr_5274] is violated.⌋
